newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Shinhan Bank shrs fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shinhan Bank shrs fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in South Korea's Shinhan Bank fell in very active Tuesday morning trading due to profit taking by domestic investors after additional shares were made available for foreign investment, brokers said.
The shares fell 300 won to 14,800 by 10:00 a.m. (0100 GMT).
An additional 1.75 percent stake in Shinhan was opened for overseas investors.

On October 1, South Korea raised the foreign stock ownership limit to 20 percent from the previous 18 percent. However, foreign investors already owned a combined 20.79 percent stake in Shinhan Bank before the ceiling rise and therefore no additional shares of the bank had been available.

After the increase in the foreign limits, 2.15 million of Shinhan Bank's 123.2 million total outstanding shares would be available to foreign investors, an official at the Securities Supervisory Board said earlier.
